spec.title: Defer tool schemas and build task-relevant agent context
spec.problem:
Chat requests send the model every tool schema (about 55 tools, roughly 9,500 tokens) and every domain protocol, even for a simple news question. Implement tool search with deferred full-schema loading inside the existing OpenAI-compatible agent loop: keep a small, locally retrieved initial tool set plus an always-available discovery tool, load full schemas only when the model asks for them, include only the domain instructions the request needs, and place stable definitions before changing state. Preserve company-identity checks, trading validation, source attribution and explicit multi-part requests. Put context selection in backend/context.js.

Interface (other code and tests depend on it):
- backend/context.js exports `createToolContext(entries, define)`. `entries` are tool metadata `{name, description, keywords?}`; `define(entry)` is async and returns the full definition with an `input_schema` (it may throw, for example when an MCP server is unavailable). It returns an object with:
  - `search(query, permitted = all names)`: ranks the permitted entries by the query's words (an exact tool name in the query ranks first), returns at most three matches as `{name, description}`, and adds them to the loaded working set (at most six tools). A query matching no permitted entry returns `[]`.
  - `async packet(permitted, required = [])`: returns `{tools, unavailable}`. `tools` starts with the always-available `tool_search` definition, followed by the full definitions of the loaded (and required) tools that are permitted; `define` is called only for those, never for the rest. Full schemas stay within about 8,000 characters in all; a tool that does not fit, or whose `define` fails, is listed in `unavailable` with a reason. `packet([])` returns `{tools: [], unavailable: []}`.
- backend/context.js exports `loopInstructions(names)`: the loop's system instructions for the given tool names. The company-identity protocol is included only when a finance/company tool is present, and the trading protocol (reserved final/holdout data, background jobs) only when a `trading_*` tool is present.
- In backend/agent.js, the loop chain's `invoke(input)` receives `input.allowed_tools` (names, always including `tool_search`) and `input.available_tools` (the serialised definitions sent to the model, under 8,500 characters for a news request, with no trading tools). A tool that `tool_search` finds is in `allowed_tools`, with its full definition in `available_tools`, on the very next step, so the model can call it then; `tool_search` calls are counted in the run's `usage` like any other tool.
- In backend/agent.js, when a tool result carries a `report` and the request asked for one deliverable, the run returns at once with `result.responses[0].report` set to that report, without another loop call, whatever the request's domain (a news request included). That applies only when the report is all that was asked for: a request for the report and something else ("market news today and the weather in London") continues to its remaining parts, and a request to explain or interpret the report continues to the model, whose answer must carry the interpretation; in both the trace's stop reason is `complete`.
acceptance_criteria: Common news prompts omit unrelated trading schemas and protocols.
Model-requested searches load only relevant authorized tool definitions.
Discovery can recover from a poor initial match and remains bounded.
Existing company and trading protections remain enforced.
A single requested report finishes without an unnecessary extra model call; multi-part goals can continue.
